# How Does AI Work? And What Are Agents? {background-color="#530153"}

## The Two Things LLMs Can Do

No matter how amazed we are with new AI capabilities the last year, the Large Language Models (LLMs) that is the technology behind text based AI, can only do these two things. And that has not changed since the publication of ChatGPT changed the world forever.

<div style="height: 1.45em;"></div>


:::: {.columns}

::: { .column width="50%" }
### Embedding Models

- Understand meaning of text, excels at:
  - Summaries
  - Finding task in prompt
  - Identify gaps in available information
- Universal topic understanding
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Generative Models

- Create text by selecting the most probable word, one word at a time
- Has generic knowledge
- Can replicate common tasks
:::

::::

## Example of the Reasoning models

:::: {.columns .v-center-container}

::: {.column width="50%" }

  ![](./img/reasoning-models.svg)

:::

::: {.column width="50%" }

### Reasoning Models

- Models review your prompt and use tools to gather additional information that "improves" your prompt
- Not a linear process - jumps back and forth as the model deems fit
- Steps are repeated until the model is satisfied

:::

::::


# Tools {background-color="#530153"}


## LLMs Cannot Do Math

### What is "3 x 7"?

::: {.fragment}
How many of you calculated it by:

- Adding 7 three times: 7 + 7 = 14, and 14 + 7 = 21
- Fetching the answer from memory
:::

::: {.fragment}

### Language models fetches from memory
LLMs can solve "3 x 7" because it appears in many multiplication tables in the training data. 

However, "35 x 22" is rarely present in multiplication tables, so LLMs do not reliably know the answer.

How can AI platforms like ChatGPT still solve 35 x 22?
:::

## But How Can AI Platforms Do Math?


AI platforms, like ChatGPT or mAI, are much more than just the model in the LLM. They have tools with instructions for when to use them.

::: {.fragment}
The model identifies the prompt is a math question. It extracts the numbers and the operator, and sends this to a calculator. The answer is then added to the prompt. 
:::
::: {.fragment}
The updated prompt becomes:
```json
{
  "human_prompt": "What is 35 x 22?",
  "calculator_tool_answer": 770
}
```
You do then not need math to generate the answer: "35 times 22 is equal to 770".
:::

::: {.fragment}
### Have you ever helped a child with math home work:

Bob, Alice, and Tom have 7 apples each. How many apples do they have together?
:::

# Agents {background-color="#530153"}

## Agents

:::: {.columns .v-center-container}

::: {.column width="65%" }

* An agent is software that combines LLM and tools.
* It uses the LLM to review a request and decide which tools to use.
* For example, a coding agent can read code files in the project folder, adding what it finds to the prompt.
* Once the model has enough context, the agent generates a response or, for coding tasks, writes code in the project folder.

:::

::: {.column width="35%" }

  ![](./img/reasoning-models.svg)

```json
{
  "human_prompt": "What is 35 x 22?",
  "calculator_tool_answer": 770
}
```

:::

::::

## What is Context Window?

:::: {.columns .v-center-container}
::: {.column width="65%" }

* In most AI requests, much more information relevant for the task is gathered in addition to what the user provides.

* This is central to why AI performs so much better today than three years ago.

* Everything sent to the generative model is called: **_the Context Window_** -- the human prompt is often only a small part of it. 

* It may include full content of project files, code outputs, and web searches. Managing the context window is central to productive and cost-effective AI use.

:::
::: {.column width="35%" }

```json
{
  "human_prompt": "What is 35 x 22?",
  "calculator_tool_answer": 770
}
```

:::
::::

## Which Agent is Best?

- Any definite answer will soon be outdated, so I won't attempt one
- Anthropic has pioneered many features, and Claude is currently a market leader
- But just as no one knew about Claude two years ago, no one knows today what tools will be the market leader in two years.
- While the details differ and the features are called different things, how to use AI, including agentic AI, comes down to managing the context window. 
- **_Prediction:_** Skills sets for managing context windows, will be essential for effective usage of AI in the future as well -- but will look and be called differently.
- Currently, ITS provisions licenses for GitHub Copilot, so that is what we will use in this training.

## Common confusions related to data privacy and AI agents

- mAI, GitHub Copilot has access to Claude models. This is **NOT** the same as using Claude Code. Claude Code is an agent -- agents combine models and tools.
- mAI sends your request to a more secure server, ensuring that sensitive information is better protected -- this **DOES NOT** transfer to GitHub Copilot or Claude Code.
- Neither GitHub Copilot or Claude Code allows you to route traffic to mAI models that are much more private.

# Context window

## What do I need to know about the Context Windows?

:::: {.columns .v-center-container}
::: {.column width="75%" }

The more information included in the context window, the better responses, right? - **NO!!**

* All context windows has a max capacity. The size of the context window depends on the model. If you surpass the limit, the AI will start making summaries of the earlier content.

* However, the closer to that limit, the less the AI can handle and keep track of details and nuances. How close you can be to the context limit depends on the specific task. 

* One character in coding can break the code, while one miscolored image pixel is not visible to the human eye.

:::
::: {.column width="25%" }

![](../img/context-window.png)

<span style="display: block; text-align: center; font-size: 0.7em; line-height: 1;">This is how we will represent context window from now on.</span>

:::
::::

## Prompt Engineering vs. Agents

Prompt Engineering was the hottest buzz word two years ago. And one central theme was to provide the AI with all relevant context in the prompt. -- That is still relevant, but the agents do much of it for us. 

### Which prompt gets the most correct and helpful answer?

**A.** Paste only the error code and ask for a solution.

**B.** Paste the error code and relevant parts of project files that could be related to the error.

Option B is a central best practice in prompt engineering. Coding agents do this best practice for you.

## Sessions

- Each chat or agent execution is called a session. Each session has its own context window.

- All back and forth between the user and the AI is included in the context window.

- If you are starting a new topic, _always_ start a new session. Otherwise, you clutter the context window which leads to loss of details -- it also saves your token credits.

- Edit and resubmit your previous prompt rather than asking the AI to "forget" previous prompts or answers.

## Planning Mode

- Use "_planning mode_" when starting a new non-trivial task. 
- In planning mode:
  - The agent stays in context gathering mode, until you indicate it should proceed.
  - The agent gathers relevant context and asks for human input instead of guessing when it cannot find relevant context 
- The agent will provide you with its plan after you have answered questions. If you spot something incorrect or missing, you can provide additional input before execution.
